description: htop for your ports. Inspect processes, Docker & systemd, detect port drift, audit Compose, and manage it all from TUI, Web or Cockpit.
name: portop
readme_text:
# portop [![CI](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/release.yml) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/padovanl/portop?sort=semver)](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/padovanl/portop/total)](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/padovanl/portop.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/padovanl/portop) [![Go version](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/padovanl/portop)](go.mod) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/padovanl/portop)](LICENSE) [![portop](https://snapcraft.io/portop/badge.svg)](https://snapcraft.io/portop) [![Homebrew](https://img.shields.io/homebrew/v/portop?logo=homebrew)](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/portop) [![APT](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapt.lucapadovan.dev%2Fbadges%2Fportop.json&logo=debian)](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html#apt) [![portop on The Terminal Index](https://cli.masoko.net/badge/portop.svg)](https://cli.masoko.net/tools/portop/) [![Microsoft Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/microsoft_store-available-0078D4)](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ319F4LW70) [![winget](https://img.shields.io/badge/winget-in_review-lightgrey)](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/pull/453604) **[Website](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/) · [Documentation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/) · [Releases](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases)**
portop is an htop-style terminal UI for the TCP and UDP sockets on a machine. For every port it shows the process, its systemd unit or Windows service, its Docker, Podman or Kubernetes container, who can reach it and what the firewall does with it, and it lets you inspect or stop the owner from the keyboard. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, in the terminal, in a browser or inside Cockpit. ![portop: the port table colored by exposure, filtering to nginx, its details with workers, the kill confirmation, sorting by exposure and the help screen](docs/assets/demo.gif) ## ✨ Features **See what is using your ports** - A live table of listening and established sockets with process, PID, CPU, user and service names (`:22 ssh`), sortable by any column. - The systemd unit or Windows service, and the Docker, Podman or Kubernetes container behind each socket, read from cgroups with no daemon of its own. - One row for a server's master and its workers: `nginx +3`. - Bytes per second for every established TCP connection (Linux, macOS). **Know who can reach them** - Listening ports colored by exposure: every interface, one address or loopback only. - The host firewall's verdict for exposed ports: allowed, restricted to some sources, or blocked. **Act on them** - Process details, and SIGTERM or SIGKILL after a confirmation that re-checks the process identity. - `--wait 5432` blocks until a service listens; `--free 3000` stops whatever holds a port and waits until it is released. - Open a port in the browser, copy a row, filter by any word. **Catch changes** - New listening ports are highlighted live, with an optional desktop notification. - `--save-baseline` and `--diff` (exit code 3) report ports that appear, disappear or become reachable from the network, from cron or CI. - `--compose DIR` checks a Docker Compose project's published ports against what actually listens. **Use it anywhere** - `--json` for scripts, a web dashboard with sign-in, TLS and Prometheus `/metrics`, and a Cockpit add-on. - 13 themes and remappable keys from a live settings screen. ## 📥 Install | System | Command | |--------|---------| | Debian, Ubuntu | [APT repository](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html#apt) | | Linux (Snap) | `sudo snap install portop` | | macOS, Linux | `brew install portop` | | Windows | `winget install padovanl.portop`, or the [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ319F4LW70) | | Linux, macOS | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/padovanl/portop/main/install.sh \| sh` | | From source | `go install github.com/padovanl/portop/cmd/portop@latest` | The APT repository serves amd64, arm64 and armhf: ```bash sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings curl -fsSL https://apt.lucapadovan.dev/lucapadovan.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/lucapadovan.gpg >/dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/lucapadovan.gpg] https://apt.lucapadovan.dev stable main" \ | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lucapadovan.list sudo apt update && sudo apt install portop ``` Release archives cover Linux on amd64, arm64, ARMv7 and ARMv6, macOS on Intel and Apple Silicon, and Windows on x64 and ARM64, with `.deb` and `.rpm` packages for Linux. See [Installation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html) for every option. ## ⌨️ Usage ```bash portop # the live table portop nginx 443 # filtered: every word must match portop --listen # listening sockets only portop --json # one snapshot for scripts portop --wait 5432 # exit 0 once something listens portop --free 3000 # stop whatever holds the port portop --save-baseline # record what listens now portop --diff # exit 3 if that changed portop --compose ./stack # audit a Compose project's ports portop --web # dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8088 ``` Run `sudo portop` (an Administrator terminal on Windows) to see other users' processes and read the firewall. In the table, press `?` for help and `,` for settings. The [documentation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/) covers every flag, the JSON fields, exit codes and what each platform supports. ![portop web dashboard: sign-in, the listening tab with exposure and firewall badges, nginx with its workers and the details dialog](docs/assets/web-dashboard.gif) ## 🆚 Why not just `ss -tlnp`? | | ss / netstat | lsof | bandwhich | portop | |----------------------------------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Live, refreshing view | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Owning process | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | systemd unit, Windows service | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Docker, Podman, Kubernetes | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Exposure and firewall verdict | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Per-connection traffic | ✅ `-ti` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Stop the owner, safely | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | `--wait` / `--free` for scripts | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Baseline drift, Compose audit | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Web dashboard, Prometheus | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Linux, macOS and Windows | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ## 📚 Documentation - [Installation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html) and [first run](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/first-run.html) - [The table](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/the-table.html): columns, colors, keys - [Command line](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/command-line.html) and [scripting](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/scripting.html) - [Baseline drift](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/baseline.html) and [Compose audit](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/compose.html) - [Containers](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/containers.html), [firewall](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/firewall.html) and [traffic](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/traffic.html) - [Web dashboard and metrics](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/web-dashboard.html), [Cockpit add-on](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/cockpit.html) - [Configuration](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/configuration.html) and [platform support](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/platforms.html) The documentation is generated from [`docs-src/`](docs-src) with `python3 scripts/build-docs.py`; preview the whole site with `python3 scripts/serve-pages.py`. ## 🤝 Contributing Pull requests are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Open them against `develop`, and run `gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test ./...` before pushing. ## 📄 License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
